fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating, atmospheric plasma spraying, or the critical 550 °C annealing intervention.
It omits the specified sulfuric-acid and 900 °C molten-salt environments and instead invokes vague chloride, process, and radiation conditions.
No prior findings or citations support the proposed hypothesis.
Changing bulk chromium content confounds passive-film chemistry with alloy composition and microstructure, so the experiment cannot uniquely establish that the Cr-rich film is the governing cause.
explanation: Chromium-rich passivation is scientifically plausible and overlaps one component of the target mechanism, which includes Cr-rich and Al-rich protective oxides. The proposed comparison also supplies measurable corrosion and surface-film outcomes plus a nominal falsification rule. However, it misses the central material system and treatment: a plasma-sprayed equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L, annealed for 2 h with an optimum at 550 °C. It also omits grain refinement, BCC/FCC phase behavior, coating porosity, sluggish diffusion, and molten-salt penetration or fluxing. Its boundaries are not operationally specified, and the broad reference to nuclear radiation is unsupported. A stronger causal design would hold alloy composition constant while manipulating or disrupting the passive film, or compare coating and annealing states while correlating oxide chemistry with polarization resistance and cyclic mass gain.
